key_big: Sort waste: wet in green, dry in blue.
body_html:
How to think about it

Waste is what we throw away. Wet waste such as peels and leftover food goes in the green bin and can become compost. Dry waste such as paper, plastic, glass and metal goes in the blue bin and much of it can be recycled. Things like peels and paper rot (they are biodegradable), but plastic, glass and metal do not.

We can make less waste by reducing (carry a cloth bag), reusing (an old jar as a pen stand) and recycling (old newspapers into new paper). Never throw waste in drains, rivers or on the road, and never burn plastic.

Example

Banana peel: green or blue bin?

it rots

Answer: green bin (wet waste)

Example

An old jar as a pen stand is…

using it again

Answer: reusing

Common mistakes

  • Putting plastic in the compost pit.
  • Burning waste to get rid of it.
  • Mixing reuse and recycle.

faq.q: What is the difference between wet and dry waste?
faq.a: Wet waste comes from food and plants and rots; dry waste such as paper, plastic, glass and metal does not rot easily.

faq.q: What do reduce, reuse and recycle mean?
faq.a: Reduce: use less. Reuse: use again. Recycle: make new things from old materials.
